The Reachability Proof

ork:verify 4.6.0 · the manifest's second axis · REACHED vs UNREACHED

The one-line version

The Verification Manifest grades who ran a claim. It never graded whether the green means anything.

The row that looks strongest and is worthless

| # | Load-bearing claim | Asserted by | Provenance | Evidence                        |
|---|--------------------|-------------|------------|---------------------------------|
| 2 | Retry logic covered| test-gen    | ✅ VERIFIED | `pytest -q` · exit 0 · 214 passed |

That row is completely honest. The lead ran the command, read the output, cited the key line. And the feature underneath it can still be entirely dead, because a suite passing does not prove the suite reached the change.

This is not hypothetical. A validator shipped 2026-07-19 was fully defined, fully tested, and never called at its call site. Every test passed while exercising the old path. The suite was green, the manifest would have read VERIFIED, and the feature was inert.

Two axes, not one

QuestionStates
Provenance
the manifest		 Did the lead run this, or relay someone else's assertion? ✅ VERIFIED · 🟡 CLAIMED · ⬜ UNCHECKED · ⚪ WAIVED
Reachability
this change		 Would this test fail if the change were absent? 🟢 REACHED · 🟡 UNREACHED · ⚪ WAIVED
A row can be VERIFIED and UNREACHED at once. That combination is the most dangerous state in the report, because it looks like the strongest one.

Try it: which mutation actually proves anything?

A new validate_portal_token() is added, and routes/portal.py is supposed to call it. Pick a mutation and see whether the test suite catches a dead call site.

Pick a mutation above.

The proof

1. COMMIT the change first.          # non-negotiable
2. Mutate the CALL SITE.             # not the new unit
3. Run the test  ->  expect RED.     # this is the proof
4. git checkout -- <mutated file>    # restores to HEAD == the committed change
5. Run the test  ->  expect GREEN.

Record both runs in the manifest row. A proof with only step 5 is not a proof.

Rule 1 · commit before mutating

git checkout -- <file> restores to HEAD, not to your pre-mutation working state. Mutating uncommitted work means step 4 reverts the mutation and the change together. This has already destroyed a real fix plus ~40 lines of a new guard in one stroke.

Rule 2 · mutate the call site

The failure being hunted is new code that is never invoked. Mutating the new unit proves only that the unit's own tests exercise the unit, which was never in doubt. It leaves the actual defect, a dead call site, completely undetected.

The verdict rule

A test added or modified by this diff that is 🟡 UNREACHED caps the verdict at IMPROVEMENTS RECOMMENDED. It cannot grade READY FOR MERGE until the proof is shown or the row is explicitly ⚪ WAIVED with a reason.

This stacks with the existing gates rather than replacing them: dimension blockers, the provenance cap, and this reachability cap must all clear. Under --streak=N an UNREACHED new test resets the streak to 0.

verify does not perform the mutation

ork:verify writes no test files and edits no source, and that contract is not relaxed here. It grades the proof; it does not produce one. The proof comes from whoever wrote the code, typically /ork:implement or /ork:cover. Absent a proof the row is UNREACHED and the verdict is capped. A skill that edited source in order to grade itself would be the same category error the proof exists to catch.

The proof caught a defect in its own PR

Running the proof against the commit that introduces it found the first commit was dead on arrival: it edited only plugins/ork/skills/verify/SKILL.md, but build-plugins.sh rsyncs src/ into plugins/, so the next build would have silently overwritten it. Every test was green throughout. 

baseline   test-skill-length.sh   exit 0   493 lines, within 520
mutated    append 120 lines       exit 1   FAIL: 614 lines
restored   test-skill-length.sh   exit 0   All skills within line limit

The first proof run came back green precisely because the gate never read the file being edited. That is the defect this axis exists to surface, found inside the change that adds it.
